description: Live record CRUD for the dv-data skill against a real Dataverse org, driven by NATURAL customer prompts -- what a real user would type, not prompt-engineered instructions (no 'write a python script', no 'optimize for fewest HTTP calls', no 'read it back and confirm'). The customer states the JOB; the assertions verify the OUTCOME and whether the agent did it the right way, efficiently. Outcome is judged from the captured tool-call RESULTS in the trajectory (returned record IDs / affected counts) -- NOT from the agent's own summary claim, and NOT by asking the agent to self-verify. Every test is fully SELF-CONTAINED and runs in isolation: tests that need existing records seed their OWN with a unique name prefix (EvalSeed / EvalUpd / EvalDel) so they never collide. Routing is capability-based per the skills (overview Hard Rule 2): small writes (<=25) may use MCP create_record, the Dataverse CLI (dataverse data ...), or the SDK as peers; bulk writes beyond 25 use the SDK's CreateMultiple/UpdateMultiple (MCP caps at 25, the CLI is single-record); the SDK has no DeleteMultiple, so bulk delete is query-then-per-ID-delete (SDK or CLI). Raw urllib/requests is rejected only where a managed surface covers the operation. Tests target out-of-box account/contact tables so runs are deterministic.
defaultAssertions: PRIORITY_2: FIRST_ATTEMPT: Agent achieved the goal on its first approach without fumbling, error-recovery pivots, or retries that indicate the skill should have guided better

All three contacts carry firstname, lastname, and emailaddress1 parsed from the natural prompt. Hand-rolled raw urllib/requests is NOT acceptable -- a managed surface covers this. The agent just does the job; it does not need to self-verify.

tests.prompt: In my Dataverse org, create 200 accounts named 'EvalUpd Account 1' through 'EvalUpd Account 200', then mark all of them as reviewed by setting their description to 'Reviewed 2026'.
tests.expected_response: Self-contained: first bulk-create the 200 EvalUpd seed accounts (SDK CreateMultiple), then bulk-UPDATE beyond 25 => SDK UpdateMultiple. To update, query the EvalUpd accounts to collect their IDs (any managed read), then pass a list of {id + description} dicts to client.records.update('account', [...]), or use the broadcast form update('account', [ids], {changes}). Only the changed field (description) should be sent -- the customer does not say that; the skill/agent should do it and the assertion checks it. Do NOT use create()/upsert() for the update step (records exist), and do NOT loop one update per record. The test seeds its own data.

tests.prompt: In my Dataverse org, create 100 accounts named 'EvalDel Account 1' through 'EvalDel Account 100', then clean them up by deleting every account whose name starts with 'EvalDel'.
tests.expected_response: Self-contained: first bulk-create the 100 EvalDel seed accounts (SDK CreateMultiple), then safe bulk delete. Delete is two steps with real managed methods only: query accounts where name starts with 'EvalDel' to collect their IDs (any managed read), then delete each by ID -- the SDK has NO DeleteMultiple, so per-ID deletes via client.records.delete('account', id) in a loop or the Dataverse CLI (dataverse data delete) per ID. Because delete is destructive, the agent should warn and ask for confirmation before executing the deletes. Do NOT invent methods like bulk_delete(), delete_where(), or purge(), and do NOT pass a list of IDs to a single delete. The test seeds its own data.
tests.description: Natural cleanup request: the test seeds its own 100 'EvalDel' accounts, then query-then-per-ID-delete (no DeleteMultiple; no invented helpers), with destructive-op confirmation. Outcome asserted from the delete tool-call results. No dependency on any other test.
